claims.text: An optimal Al concentration in single-phase CrFeCoNiAl selectively produces a continuous, coherent α-Al2O3 scale above 900 °C.
The α-Al2O3 scale minimizes oxygen-ion diffusion.
The α-Al2O3 scale minimizes interfacial stresses.
Selective Al oxidation suppresses less-protective oxides formed by the other alloying elements.
Suppressing competing oxides prevents cracking and spallation of the scale.
The investigated materials will be homogenized, initially oxide-free, single-phase CrFeCoNi-based alloys with systematically varied Al additions.
Quantifying Cr- or Ni-containing secondary oxides while varying Al can isolate the effect of selective Al oxidation.
The relevant exposure range is 900–1000 °C for 100–500 hours under isothermal oxidizing or corrosive conditions.
A continuous, well-adherent α-Al2O3 scale at the metal–oxide interface acts as a barrier to further oxidation.
Selective oxidation of Al nucleates and grows low-diffusivity α-Al2O3.
Crystallographic compatibility between α-Al2O3 and CrFeCoNiAl minimizes interfacial stress.
An optimal Al concentration will produce a slower-growing scale with lower crack density and greater spallation resistance than a low-Al alloy.
Low-Al CrFeCoNiAl forms mixed, non-protective oxide scales.
The low-Al baseline forms unstable, cracking scales because mixed oxides from multiple alloying elements predominate.
The hypothesis applies only to single-phase CrFeCoNiAl under 900–1000 °C oxidative conditions and excludes multiphase alloys and Si- or Mn-containing variants.
Failure of higher Al content to yield a continuous Al2O3 scale with reduced crack density, or dominance by secondary oxides, would falsify the hypothesis.
